title: Site exchange comparisons under the smooth orientation
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix the six-functor datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum] with its bounded constructible finite-Tor domains [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $X$ be a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension $d\geq0$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $a_X:X\to s$ its structure morphism. No descent of $X$ to a finite field and no properness is assumed. Use the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and coefficient twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Set
$$H_\Lambda=\Lambda_X(d)[2d],\quad\omega_\Lambda=Ra_X^!\Lambda_s,\quad\gamma_\Lambda:H_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_\Lambda,\quad\eta_\Lambda=\gamma_\Lambda^{-1},$$
where $\gamma$ is the stipulated smooth purity map [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], reconstructed integrally and rationalized or taken at a common finite field stage as in [def-pur-conventions].

For a stipulated coefficient change $Q_W$ on $W=X,s$, namely finite reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ ($1\leq m\leq n$), integral reduction, integral coefficient-field extension, rationalization, or common finite-field-stage extension, let $h_Q:Q_XH_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{\Lambda'}$ be the tensor/twist/shift comparison and $z_Q:Q_X\omega_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{\Lambda'}$ the exceptional-adjunction comparison at the unit. Then, for the specified simultaneous purity family,
$$z_Q\circ Q_X(\gamma_\Lambda)=\gamma_{\Lambda'}\circ h_Q,\qquad h_Q\circ Q_X(\eta_\Lambda)=\eta_{\Lambda'}\circ z_Q.$$
The integral reduction uses the specified normalized reconstruction, integral extension uses its scalar-natural family, and the field maps are its rationalized and common-stage maps; the assertion does not concern arbitrary choices of lifts of finite-level isomorphisms.

Suppose additionally that $a_X$ is exceptionally admissible at the stages in use [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be site-perfect [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Put $K'=Q_XK$, $C=Ra_{X!}K$, $C'=Ra_{X!}K'$, $D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega_\Lambda)$, and $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,R\operatorname{id}_s^!\Lambda_s)$. Let $e_\Lambda:D_sC\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X*}D_XK$ be the canonical exchange [fix-cor-verdier-exchange], $u_Q:Q_sC\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$ the compact-support comparison, and $\delta_{Q,C}:Q_sD_sC\to D_sQ_sC$ the internal-Hom comparison. Let $R_Q:Q_sRa_{X*}D_XK\to Ra_{X*}D_XK'$ be ordinary-direct-image comparison followed by internal-Hom comparison and $z_Q$. Then
$$R_Q\circ Q_s(e_\Lambda)=e_{\Lambda'}\circ D_s(u_Q^{-1})\circ\delta_{Q,C}.$$
The maps here are the actual tensor, internal-Hom, evaluation and adjunction comparisons. At finite quotients the internal-Hom comparison on $X$ uses the site-perfect first variable $K$; the point internal Hom and finite-quotient ordinary direct image use the finite-Tor comparisons, not an ordinary-direct-image assertion of the elementary operation-reduction lemma. Integral objects are derived-complete, and the field operations use the stipulated rationalization and common-stage constructions.

Put $P_\Lambda(K)=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,H_\Lambda)$ and $\theta_\Lambda=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\eta_\Lambda):D_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_\Lambda(K)$. The same square, transported by $Ra_{X*}\theta_\Lambda$ and $Ra_{X*}\theta_{\Lambda'}$, is the canonical coefficient square with the smooth orientation inserted: its right comparison is the tensor/internal-Hom comparison into $P_{\Lambda'}(K')$. Thus this transported comparison is the specified oriented comparison, not merely a conjugate with an unspecified identification.

source.place: Second paragraph: site-perfect operation comparisons, smooth dualizing object and counit reduction, and composition of the coefficient-change comparisons.

proof.text: Apply [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] to $f=a_X$ and the coefficient unit on $s$. Its vertical arrows are the six-operation finite-reduction maps of [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons]: on $Lf^*K(d)[2d]$ the pullback, twist and shift comparison, which at the coefficient unit is $h_Q$, and on $Rf^!K$ the unique arrow whose compact-support transpose is the reduced counit, which at the unit is the exceptional-adjunction comparison $z_Q$. So the theorem gives $z_Q Q_X\gamma_\Lambda=\gamma_{\Lambda'}h_Q$ for finite quotients. All hypotheses hold: $a_X$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$, both schemes are separated finite type over $k$, and the coefficient unit has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. This uses the diagonal-purity reduction theorem, without a properness or finite-field-descent hypothesis. For any coefficient square of this form, compose on the left with $\eta_{\Lambda'}$ and on the right with $Q_X\eta_\Lambda$. The two inverse identities give $\eta_{\Lambda'}z_Q=h_Q Q_X\eta_\Lambda$. Thus the inverse square follows from the forward square, for every stage treated below.

source.place: Second paragraph: site-perfect operation comparisons, smooth dualizing object and counit reduction, and composition of the coefficient-change comparisons.

proof.text: For integral reduction, [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] says that the specified integral purity map reduces to exactly the finite purity map under the canonical comparisons, at every $n$. This is the required forward square. Use the simultaneous family specified in the question: [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] supplies its integral-extension equation $b\,C(\gamma_E)=\gamma_F a$. At the coefficient unit its $a$ is $h_Q$, and its $b$ is $z_Q$: the statement explicitly defines $b$ as the exceptional-adjunction transpose of scalar extension of the counit after the inverse compact-support comparison. It also identifies completed integral scalar extension with ordinary derived tensor. Therefore its equation is precisely our integral-extension square. No uniqueness of lifts or inference of equality of integral maps from equality of all reductions is used.

source.place: Second paragraph: site-perfect operation comparisons, smooth dualizing object and counit reduction, and composition of the coefficient-change comparisons.

proof.text: At rationalization, [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] identifies the purity map with rationalization of the adic map. [lem-pur-rational-scalar-comparison-identification] identifies the localized source comparison with the specified tensor/twist/shift comparison and the localized exceptional comparison with the counit-preserving mate. Applying rationalization to the integral square consequently gives the square with $h_Q,z_Q$, including finite field extensions. For a common-stage extension use [lem-pur-common-stage-smooth-operation-identification]: its two functors and their map actions are the stipulated smooth and exceptional operations, and equations of compatible transformations retain their finite-stage representatives. Represent our square at a common finite field; it is the preceding rational square there, and hence is the asserted square in the common-stage category. Step 1's inverse calculation applies to each of these squares.

source.place: Second paragraph: site-perfect operation comparisons, smooth dualizing object and counit reduction, and composition of the coefficient-change comparisons.

proof.text: Now assume the exceptional admissibility and site-perfect hypotheses on $K$ in the question. [thm-sf-ctf-stability] gives the bounded constructible finite-Tor domains for $C=Ra_{X!}K$, $D_XK$ and their ordinary direct images at finite level, and its higher-stage clauses give the derived-complete, rational and common-stage domains. In particular the coefficient unit, its exceptional image, and the internal Homs used here lie in the indicated domains. For finite quotients the comparison on $X$ is the evaluation-transpose isomorphism of [lem-fix-site-perfect-scalar-hom], applied with first variable $K$. The point comparison is the finite-Tor internal-Hom map of [thm-coef-finite-hom], applied on $s$ to $C$ and the point dualizing object. The ordinary-direct-image comparison for $D_XK$ is [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], in its explicitly stated pro-etale form. These statements do not require the quotient ring to be flat. All other operation comparisons, their evaluations and adjunction units and counits are those preserved by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. In particular we do not infer finite-quotient ordinary-direct-image comparison from that elementary operation lemma.

source.place: Second paragraph: site-perfect operation comparisons, smooth dualizing object and counit reduction, and composition of the coefficient-change comparisons.

proof.text:
Apply [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] to $f=a_X$ and $Y=s$. Its structure maps are $a_X$ and $\operatorname{id}_s$. The latter has the identity adjunction, cohomological-dimension bound zero and zero interval shifts, so is admissible; $a_X$ is admissible by hypothesis. The exchange is the canonical evaluation-transposed one of [def-sf-verdier-exchange-data]. Its asserted coefficient compatibility is therefore the square for the actual dual scalar arrows and counit-normalized ordinary-direct-image arrow defined there. Its source is $Q_sD_sC$ and its target is $Ra_{X*}D_XK'$. On the source, evaluation coefficient change gives $\delta_{Q,C}$; changing the compact-support input from $Q_sC$ to $C'$ gives precomposition by $u_Q^{-1}$, namely $D_s(u_Q^{-1})$. On the target the ordinary-direct-image arrow followed by Hom comparison and the dualizing mate is exactly $R_Q$. Thus the compatibility assertion, with these endpoints and the stipulated comparisons verified in step 4, reads
$$R_Q Q_s(e_\Lambda)=e_{\Lambda'}D_s(u_Q^{-1})\delta_{Q,C}.$$
This also fixes the direction of $u_Q^{-1}$; contravariance would make $D_s(u_Q)$ have the wrong source.

source.place: Second paragraph: site-perfect operation comparisons, smooth dualizing object and counit reduction, and composition of the coefficient-change comparisons.

proof.text:
Write $c_\omega:Q_XD_XK\to D_XK'$ and $c_H:Q_XP_\Lambda(K)\to P_{\Lambda'}(K')$ for evaluation-transposed Hom comparison followed by $z_Q$ and $h_Q$, respectively. Naturality in the second Hom variable, with step 1's inverse square, gives
$$c_H Q_X(\theta_\Lambda)=\theta_{\Lambda'}c_\omega.$$
Explicitly, transpose both sides: their evaluations are coefficient-changed evaluation into $Q_X\omega_\Lambda$ followed by $h_Q Q_X\eta_\Lambda$, respectively by $\eta_{\Lambda'}z_Q$. These are equal by the already proved square, so the adjunction bijection gives equality of the arrows. The evaluation-preserving comparisons, natural in the second Hom variable, are those of [lem-fix-site-perfect-scalar-hom] on $X$ at finite quotients (first variable $K$) and of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] at the other stages. Let $b_T:Q_sRa_{X*}T\to Ra_{X*}Q_XT$ be the ordinary comparison. Its naturality ([lem-coef-finite-direct-image] at finite quotients, [lem-fix-operation-reduction] otherwise) gives $b_P Q_s(Ra_{X*}\theta)=Ra_{X*}(Q_X\theta)b_D$. Consequently, for $R_Q^H=Ra_{X*}(c_H)b_P$, the preceding equality gives
$$R_Q^H Q_s(Ra_{X*}\theta_\Lambda)=Ra_{X*}(\theta_{\Lambda'})R_Q.$$
Compose step 5's square with $Ra_{X*}\theta_{\Lambda'}$ and substitute this identity. The resulting square is the oriented square, and its right arrow is $R_Q^H$, the specified tensor/internal-Hom comparison into $P_{\Lambda'}(K')$. This calculation identifies the arrow itself rather than only its source and target.
